Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · School & learning

knowledge noun

what one knows, learning

also learning, general knowledge, thirst for knowledge, knowledge of

classical

Cic. Off. 1.18: ad cognitiōnis et scientiae cupiditātem
Caes. BG 3.8.1: scientiā atque ūsū rērum nauticārum
Traupman 337, 155

scientia, scientiae f.

noun, first declension

knowledge (of a subject), knowing

What one knows goes in the genitive (scientia rērum nauticārum). Set against ūsus, practice, it is knowledge in theory (Cic. Rep. 1.2; see theory).

Other words

  • cognitiō, cognitiōnis f. — getting to know, knowledge gained

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.153: cognitiō contemplātiōque nātūrae; Traupman 337, 155

    Traupman’s word for “acquisition of knowledge” (p. 337).

  • doctrīna, doctrīnae f. — learning, what one has been taught

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 6.12.5: est ūnum perfugium doctrīna ac litterae

Examples

  • Omnēs enim trahimur et dūcimur ad cognitiōnis et scientiae cupiditātem, in quā excellere pulchrum putāmus

    for we are all drawn and led to the desire for learning and knowledge, and we think it a fine thing to excel in itCic. Off. 1.18

  • sed est ūnum perfugium doctrīna ac litterae, quibus semper ūsī sumus

    but there is one refuge, learning and books, which we have always made use ofCic. Fam. 6.12.5

See also know, learn, experience, information, knowledge, theory.
